questions.question: Dr. Mamouni practices as a natural person. According to the Code of Ethics, is his activity considered a commercial activity?
options: Yes, because he receives fees
No, he practices a non-commercial liberal profession
Yes, because he is subject to the Commercial Code
No, because he does not have a professional premises
questions.explanation: The Code of Ethics for dentists (Decree No. 2-96-989) specifies that the profession of dental surgeon is a liberal profession. He cannot behave as a merchant and commercial advertising is prohibited.

questions.question: If the liberal profession is not commercial, why must Dr. Ibrahimi register with the Trade Register?
options: To obtain merchant status
To comply with accounting and tax obligations
To be able to invoice his patients
To become president of the Order
questions.explanation: Despite his liberal status, the dentist is considered a merchant in the formal sense of the law. Registration with the Trade Register is the consequence of the accounting and tax obligations defined by the Commercial Code.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, a natural person, is responsible for the debts of his activity on:
options: Only his professional assets
All his personal assets
Only his initial contribution
No assets, the State is guarantor
questions.explanation: As a natural person, there is no legal distinction between personal and professional assets. The dentist is responsible for his debts on all his assets. This is the principle of unlimited liability.

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi is considering creating an LLC for his practice. According to Law 5-96, what is the main advantage of this structure?
options: Simplification of tax declarations
Limitation of liability to contributions
Total tax exemption
Obligation not to have employees
questions.explanation: Law 5-96 on LLCs is based on the principle of limited liability. Partners are only liable for company debts up to the amount of their contributions, thus protecting their personal assets.

questions.question: According to the Commercial Code, can Dr. Mamouni, as a natural person, open a personal bank account for his professional activity?
options: Yes, it's the simplest
No, he must open a separate professional bank account
Yes, if the bank agrees
No, because he is not entitled to have an account
questions.explanation: The Commercial Code requires merchants to open a professional bank account for their business transactions, to ensure traceability of financial flows.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni and his colleague wish to associate. What is the most suitable and common legal form for a dental practice in Morocco?
options: A Public Limited Company (SA)
A General Partnership (SNC)
A Limited Liability Company (LLC)
A simple association contract
questions.explanation: The LLC is the most common legal form in Morocco. It offers a flexible framework with limited liability to contributions, ideal for professionals wishing to associate while protecting their personal assets.

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi creates an LLC. What is the minimum share capital required by Law 5-96?
options: 1 Dirham
questions.explanation: Law 5-96 allows the formation of an LLC with a symbolic share capital of 1 Dirham. This flexibility makes business creation accessible to all.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni is the sole partner of a single-member LLC. According to the texts, what happens in the event of death?
options: The company is automatically dissolved
An heir may request the appointment of a representative to convene the AG within 60 days
The company is transferred directly to the spouse
The activity is permanently suspended
questions.explanation: A recent amendment to Law 5-96 provides that in the event of death of the sole partner, an heir may request the court to appoint a representative to convene a general meeting to update the articles of association, within a period of 60 days.

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, a partner in an LLC, wishes to withdraw. What happens to his share of capital?
options: It is permanently lost
It is reimbursed or transferred according to the articles of association
It is given to the Order of Dentists
It automatically reverts to the manager
questions.explanation: Shares in an LLC represent a patrimonial value. In the event of withdrawal, the partner(s) may, in accordance with the articles of association, have them reimbursed or transferred to a third party.

questions.question: Is Dr. Mamouni, as a natural person, subject to the Commercial Code?
options: No, because he is a dentist
Yes, for his formal management obligations
No, because the Code of Ethics protects him
Yes, but only if he is a merchant by profession
questions.explanation: Although ethics considers him a liberal professional, the Commercial Code applies to the dentist for his formal obligations such as keeping accounts, registration, or payment of professional tax.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of partners to form a standard LLC in Morocco?
options: Unlimited
questions.explanation: The LLC is a structure that can accommodate from 2 to 50 partners, making it suitable for medium-sized practices and entrepreneurial projects.

questions.question: In an LLC, to what extent are partners liable for the company's debts?
options: On all their personal assets
Up to the amount of their capital contribution
Up to the year's profit
They are never liable
questions.explanation: The liability of partners is limited to the amount of their contributions. This is the fundamental principle of the Limited Liability Company.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni creates a single-member LLC. This legal form combines which advantage of the natural person and the LLC?
options: Protection of personal assets and simplicity of management
Collective management and unlimited liability
Commercial advertising and absence of taxes
Automatic dissolution and exemption from contributions
questions.explanation: The single-member LLC allows the sole entrepreneur to benefit from the protection of personal assets (as in an LLC) while maintaining the simplicity of management of an individual structure.

questions.question: According to the Code of Ethics, can Dr. Ibrahimi advertise his practice using commercial discounts?
options: Yes, to attract new patients
No, commercial advertising is prohibited
Yes, if approved by the Order
No, but he can post offers on social media
questions.explanation: The Code of Ethics prohibits any commercial advertising. The dentist cannot engage in mercantile practices such as loyalty discounts.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni's LLC is created. According to Law 5-96, who can be the manager of the company?
options: Only the dentist holding the diploma
A partner or an external person
A member of the Order of Dentists
A CNSS agent
questions.explanation: The articles of association of an LLC may entrust management to one or more partners, or to a person outside the company.

questions.question: Can Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, deduct personal expenses from his professional income?
options: Yes, all personal expenses
No, only professional expenses are deductible
Yes, if justified by an invoice
No, no expenses are deductible
questions.explanation: In accounting, only expenses incurred for the professional activity are deductible. Personal expenses must be borne by the private assets.

questions.question: Can a dentist in an LLC benefit from the BNC (Non-Commercial Profits) tax regime?
options: Yes, like all dentists
No, an LLC is subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
Yes, if he practices as a natural person
No, only public legal entities
questions.explanation: The BNC regime is reserved for natural persons (sole proprietorship). An LLC, as a legal entity, is subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT).

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni opts for the single-member LLC. How many partners does this legal form allow?
options: 2 partners minimum
1 sole partner
5 partners minimum
50 partners maximum
questions.explanation: The single-member LLC (LLC with a Sole Partner) is a particular form of LLC that allows a single partner to form the company.

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, who practices as a natural person, has merchant status for his formal obligations. Does this mean he is a 'merchant' in the common sense?
options: Yes, he can engage in commercial advertising
No, it is a legal fiction for management obligations
Yes, he can speculate on his business assets
No, he is not subject to VAT
questions.explanation: The qualification of merchant by the Commercial Code is a legal fiction that only concerns management acts and formal obligations. It does not modify the liberal and ethical status of the dentist.

questions.question: In the event of a dispute, can a creditor seize the personal assets of Dr. Mamouni if he is a natural person?
options: No, his professional assets are protected
Yes, because there is confusion of assets
No, the LLC offers this protection
Yes, but only if the dispute is of a tax nature
questions.explanation: As a natural person, personal and professional assets are not distinct. A creditor can therefore seize the dentist's personal assets to settle a professional debt.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni creates an LLC with his colleague. Who sets the rules of operation and profit distribution?
options: The commercial court
The National Order of Dentists
The articles of association drafted by the partners
The Ministry of Health
questions.explanation: The articles of association of the LLC, freely drafted by the partners within the framework of the law, set the rules of operation, profit distribution, and decision-making.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a standard LLC and a single-member LLC?
options: The minimum capital is higher in a single-member LLC
The number of partners (1 for the single-member LLC)
The single-member LLC is exempt from CIT
The standard LLC must file a balance sheet every month
questions.explanation: The standard LLC can have between 2 and 50 partners. The single-member LLC is a variant that allows a single person to form a limited liability company.

questions.question: Must Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, keep accounts?
options: No, he is not required to
Yes, in accordance with Law 9-88
No, because he is a dentist
Yes, but only if he is contracted
questions.explanation: Law 9-88 on the accounting obligations of merchants applies to dentists as it does to other merchants. They must therefore keep accounts.

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni wishes to open an LLC. In which register must he register?
options: Patient Register
Trade Register
Conventions Register
Diplomas Register
questions.explanation: Any commercial company, including an LLC, must be registered with the Trade Register. This registration confers legal personality on the company.

questions.question: Can Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, take out professional civil liability insurance?
options: No, only an LLC can take it out
Yes, it is a legal obligation for all dentists
No, because the risk is zero
Yes, but it is not mandatory
questions.explanation: Taking out professional civil liability insurance is a legal obligation for any health professional, regardless of their status (natural person or LLC).
